title: Spawning (spawn/1 vs. spawn/3), PIDs (self/0) & Asynchronous Message Passing (!)

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does an Erlang process need to include `self()` inside its request message tuple when communicating with an actor?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% Sending a request to a worker:
WorkerPid ! {calculate_tax, self(), OrderTotal}.

options.label: The BEAM message passing mechanism does not include implicit return addresses; the recipient actor cannot know where to send its reply unless the caller explicitly passes its PID.
options.explanation: Correct! Erlang messages are raw terms placed into mailboxes. Because the runtime does not attach caller metadata to messages, request-reply protocols must explicitly pass self() so the responder knows the destination PID.

options.label: The BEAM will crash with a badarg error if an outgoing message tuple does not contain a PID.
options.explanation: Any valid Erlang term can be sent via !. Including self() is a protocol convention for replies, not a syntax requirement.

options.label: Including self() locks the recipient process so no other process can message it.
options.explanation: Erlang processes never lock. Other processes can send messages to WorkerPid concurrently without contention.
